core_obligations: Rewrite the assertion as the bijectivity of the map from morphisms out of the spectrum of R to the inverse limit of the morphism sets over the quotients of R by the powers of the maximal ideal (proof lines 7240-7244).

Injectivity: form the fibre product of the spectrum of R with the space over the pair of morphisms and the diagonal, note that it is a locally Noetherian scheme over the spectrum of R whose point over the closed point has a local ring with the same quotients as R, and conclude by injectivity of the completion map that the local ring is R, so the two morphisms agree (proof lines 7246-7262).

Surjectivity, choice of cover and of a point upstairs: pick a surjective etale morphism from a scheme, observe that its fibre over the residue field is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions, and choose a finite separable extension of the residue field together with a compatible point of the cover (proof lines 7264-7284).

Surjectivity, lifting: form the finite etale extension of complete local rings inducing the chosen residue field extension, use formal etaleness of the cover to lift the given compatible family to the extension, and apply the scheme case of the statement to obtain a morphism from the spectrum of the extension (proof lines 7285-7296).

Surjectivity, descent: note that the tensor square of the extension is a finite product of complete local Noetherian rings to which the discussion applies, use the injectivity half to see that the two composites agree, and descend along the fppf covering given by the extension to get a morphism from the spectrum of R (proof lines 7297-7309).
Supply the verification that the given compatible family is the restriction of the descended morphism, which the author declines to prove in this span (proof lines 7309-7310).

difficulty_reason: For a complete local Noetherian algebra R over a scheme S and an algebraic space X over S, the lemma asserts that the natural map from morphisms of the spectrum of R into X to morphisms of the formal spectrum of R into X is bijective (statement lines 7226-7236). The proof rewrites the target as the inverse limit of the morphism sets over the quotients of R by powers of the maximal ideal and then proves the two halves by different mechanisms. Injectivity measures the difference of two morphisms by the fibre product with the diagonal: what results is a scheme, locally of finite type, separated and locally quasi-finite over the spectrum of R, hence locally Noetherian, and the point over the closed point has a local ring whose quotients by the powers of the maximal ideal agree with those of R; since the local ring embeds in its completion, the local ring is R and the two morphisms agree (proof lines 7240-7262). Surjectivity is a lifting argument: a surjective etale cover of the space is chosen, the fibre of that cover over the residue field is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions so that a suitable finite separable extension and a compatible point are available, the corresponding finite etale extension of complete local rings is formed, formal etaleness of the cover lifts the given compatible family to the extension, the scheme case of the statement produces a morphism from the extended spectrum, and descent along the resulting fppf covering produces a morphism from the spectrum of R (proof lines 7264-7309). The claim is H3: injectivity rests on a completion argument through a fibre product with the diagonal, surjectivity on an etale lifting combined with fppf descent, and the compatibility needed to make the descent work is obtained by invoking the injectivity half again for the tensor square of the extension -- three separate ingredients rather than one.
